sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The tests pass with this command, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\b\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass (`test_rejects_non_positive_amount` and `test_transfer_preserves_total`).

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package sits under `src/` and isn't installed, so Python can't find it. I didn't change any files.

In PowerShell or cmd, `PYTHONPATH=src` won't work as a prefix. Use one of these instead:
- PowerShell: `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`
- cmd: `set PYTHONPATH=src && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`

actions.command: cd <run>/work/L1/b/w && PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v 2>&1 | tail -15

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. The full suite passes (3 tests, including the new one).

The new test, `test_close_requires_zero_balance` in `tests/test_ledger.py`, covers three cases:
- Closing an account with a non-zero balance raises `ValueError`, and the account stays open.
- Closing the same account after its balance returns to zero succeeds.
- The closed account is removed from `ledger.accounts`.

Closing an account that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does. I didn't convert it to `ValueError` since you didn't ask for that.
